name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkish lira near record low of 50 per dollar in managed depreciation; no major EM default or IMF rescue
state: The Turkish lira traded near 50 per US dollar, a record low, on 3 Nov as authorities allowed a controlled pace of depreciation and intervened to prevent a sharper fall; October inflation rose to 29.77% (Trading Economics). Indonesia's rupiah slid to 18,160 per dollar on 2 Nov, close to its June record low (The Edge Malaysia). Neither has fallen 10% in a month, and searches on 14 Nov found no major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support.
for_you: Weaker currencies in Turkey and Indonesia raise import costs for households there and make dollar debts harder to service. Travellers to these countries may find local prices lower in their own currency.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month, no emergency IMF request, default or capital controls

sources.title: Trading Economics — Turkish lira holds at record lows
The Edge Malaysia — Singapore stocks skid as bank results loom; Jakarta rebounds

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
